reading.p: This lesson confesses one God in three Hypostases. We begin with the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, who reveals the unity of the Godhead, and we hold this faith as the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church.

reading.quote: I and My Father are one.

reading.p: Through this lesson we aim to understand several truths about God and our response to Him.

list: One God: Oriental Orthodoxy is fully monotheistic.
Three Hypostases: we believe in the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
Unity without separation: the Three are distinct, but never divided.
A revealed mystery: this is known through Scripture and the Church.
The Trinity at work: in creation, salvation, and sanctification.
Our response: worship, faith, prayer, and holy living.

reading.p: Many people misunderstand Christianity and accuse Christians of worshiping three gods. The Church teaches clearly that we believe in One God. The one true God exists eternally as the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. This truth is revealed by God through Holy Scripture and preserved in the faith of the Church.

reading.h2: Our Faith Begins with One God

reading.p: The Christian faith is completely monotheistic. Scripture affirms this again and again, and the Orthodox Creed itself begins by confessing one God.

reading.quote: Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one.
You believe that there is one God. You do well.

reading.p: The Orthodox Creed also begins: “Truly we believe in one God…”
It is important to state clearly both what we reject and what we confess.

list: Three gods
Three separate divine beings
One God divided into parts
One Person merely pretending to be three persons
One God
One divine essence
Three Hypostases: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit

reading.quote: Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

reading.p: Notice that Christ says “in the name” — one divine Name — which shows the unity of the one God. Yet He names the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, which shows the distinction of the three Hypostases. This was revealed by Christ Himself: one Name, three Hypostases.

Hypostasis is a Greek theological term. In Orthodox teaching, it refers to a real personal distinction within the One God. It can be understood as a distinct personal reality or personal property within the one divine nature. The three Hypostases are not separate gods; they are the eternal personal realities of the One God — the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

list: The Father: the origin, source, and fountainhead.
The Son: the Word, the divine intellect, begotten of the Father.
The Holy Spirit: the giver of life, proceeding from the Father, the Spirit of life.

reading.p: These names are not human inventions. Christ Himself gives them in Matthew 28:19.

When we speak about the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, we must be careful. We reject any idea that one is greater or lesser than another, such as the Father being “more divine,” the Son being “less divine,” or the Holy Spirit being a lesser force.
The Three are equal in honor, divinity, essence, eternity, glory, and worship.

The Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are distinct, but never separated. The Son is in the Father, the Father is in the Son, and the Holy Spirit is with the Father and the Son. The Three are always united in essence, will, power, and divine action.

reading.quote: I am in the Father, and the Father in Me.

reading.h2: No One Comes Before the Other in Time

reading.p: The Father never existed without the Son or the Holy Spirit. There was never a time when the Father was without His Word or without His Spirit, and never a time when the Son or the Holy Spirit did not exist. Like a candle, where flame and light come together and neither precedes the other, the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are eternal together.

A human person has an inner existence, an intellect, and a life or liveliness. This helps show unity and distinction, for the mind is not separated from the person, yet God remains greater than every comparison.
Every analogy is limited. We use it humbly, not as a full explanation of God.

The sun can also help us understand unity and distinction. The sun has a disc of fire, light, and heat. These are distinct in effect, yet not separated from the sun — a limited analogy for the Trinity. Likewise, the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are distinct, but not separated.

reading.h2: The Role of the Holy Trinity in Our Life

reading.p: The Trinity is not only a doctrine to memorize. The Holy Trinity is active in our salvation.

list: The Father wills and sends.
The Son redeems and restores.
The Holy Spirit sanctifies and gives life.
Chose us in Christ
Destined us in love to be His children
Called us
Created all things
Receives us when we repent

reading.quote: He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world.

reading.p: Related references: Ephesians 1:3–5 and Romans 8:30.

list: Gives life
Redeems us
Forgives sins
Restores the image of God in man
Became man for our salvation

reading.quote: In Him was life, and the life was the light of men.
In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of sins.

reading.h2: The Work of the Holy Spirit

list: Gives new birth
Sanctifies us
Convicts the world of sin
Comforts us
Raises our worship to God

reading.quote: Unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God.
He will convict the world of sin.
In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

reading.p: In Orthodox life, baptism is not only symbolic. It is the new birth by water and the Spirit. Through baptism, we are united to Christ, receive new life, and enter the life of the Church.

list: False: Christians believe in three gods. Truth: We believe in One God.
False: The Three are just three names for one Person. Truth: They are three real Hypostases.
False: The Son and Holy Spirit are created beings. Truth: They are eternal and divine.
False: The Trinity can be fully explained by human logic. Truth: The Trinity is a divine mystery revealed by God.

reading.p: We worship One God. This One God is not alone or lifeless; He is eternally Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. The Father is the source, the Son is begotten of the Father, and the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father. They are distinct in Hypostasis, but one in essence, divinity, glory, and worship.
The Nicene Creed is the official statement of faith of the Church. It clearly defines what we believe about God, especially about the Trinity.

reading.quote: We believe in one God, God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth, and of all things visible and invisible. And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, begotten of the Father before all worlds; Light of Light, very God of very God, begotten, not made, being of one essence with the Father; by whom all things were made; Who for us men and for our salvation came down from heaven, and was incarnate of the Holy Spirit and of the Virgin Mary, and became man; And was crucified for us under Pontius Pilate, and suffered and was buried; And the third day He rose again, according to the Scriptures; And ascended into heaven, and sits at the right hand of the Father; And He shall come again with glory to judge the living and the dead; whose kingdom shall have no end. And we believe in the Holy Spirit, the Lord, the Giver of Life, who proceeds from the Father; who with the Father and the Son together is worshipped and glorified; who spoke by the prophets. And in one holy catholic and apostolic Church. We acknowledge one baptism for the remission of sins. We look for the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the world to come. Amen.

reading.p: The Creed was established during two major Church councils: the First Council of Nicaea and the First Council of Constantinople. Their purpose was to defend the truth about Christ, to reject false teachings such as denying Christ’s divinity, and to unite the Church in one clear belief.
Because God is Trinity, our whole life is shaped by this faith.

list: We worship one God with reverence: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, one in essence and glory.
We pray in a Trinitarian way: to the Father, through the Son, in the Holy Spirit.
We live in communion, because God Himself is eternal love and communion.
We guard the true faith, rejecting confusion, false teaching, and the idea of “three gods.”
We confess with confidence the faith revealed by Christ, taught by the apostles, and preserved by the Church.
We seek holiness, allowing the Holy Spirit to sanctify us and draw us into the life of God.
Why do some people misunderstand the Trinity as belief in three gods?
How does Matthew 28:19 show both unity and distinction?
Why is it important to say the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are distinct but not separated?
Which analogy helps you most: man, the sun, or the candle? Why?
How does the doctrine of the Trinity affect the way we pray and worship?

reading.quote: I and My Father are one.

reading.p: Reflection question: What does this verse teach us about the unity of the Father and the Son?

We believe in One God in Three Hypostases. We do not worship three gods; we worship the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit — one in essence, divinity, glory, and worship. The Trinity is a mystery, but it is not confusion. It is the true faith revealed by Christ, taught by the apostles, preserved by the Church, and confessed in the Orthodox Creed.

The final takeaway is this: the Holy Trinity teaches us that God is One, eternal, living, loving, and revealed to us as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. To know the Trinity is not only to know a doctrine; it is to enter the life, worship, and salvation given to us by the One true God.

studyGuide.overview: This lesson teaches that the Christian faith is fully monotheistic: we worship One God who exists eternally as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit — three distinct Hypostases who are one in essence, divinity, glory, and worship. It shows how the Trinity is revealed in Scripture, guarded by the Nicene Creed, active in our salvation, and lived out in worship, prayer, and holiness.
keyPoints: There is only One God; belief in the Trinity is not belief in three gods.
The one God is eternally three Hypostases: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, distinct but never separated.
The Three are equal in honor, divinity, essence, eternity, glory, and worship, and none precedes another in time.
Matthew 28:19 shows both unity (one Name) and distinction (three Hypostases).
The Trinity is active in our lives: the Father wills and sends, the Son redeems and restores, the Holy Spirit sanctifies and gives life.
The Nicene Creed, from the Councils of Nicaea and Constantinople, is the Church’s official confession of this faith.
The Trinity is a revealed mystery, not a human invention or a puzzle to be fully solved by logic.
reviewQuestions: What does it mean to say Christianity is monotheistic while confessing the Trinity?
How does Matthew 28:19 reveal both the unity and the distinction in God?
Why must we say the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are distinct but never separated?
What is the specific work of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit in our salvation?
Why does the Church use analogies such as the sun, the candle, or man only humbly and not as full explanations?

checks: Strict monotheism affirmed; three gods explicitly rejected
One essence / three Hypostases (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) affirmed
Co-equality and co-eternity of the Three affirmed; subordinationism rejected
Son and Holy Spirit confessed as eternal and divine, not created (anti-Arian, anti-Macedonian)
Holy Spirit confessed as proceeding from the Father alone — no Filioque present
Nicene-Constantinopolitan Creed cited in its Father-only procession form, consistent with the first three Ecumenical Councils
Distinction without separation affirmed; modalism (‘three names for one Person’) rejected
